themes_detail.label: Graffiti explosion this week
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 26 THIS WEEK—a 1980% spike from the 1.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign or rapid deterioration of enforcement in East Flatbush.
evidence: 26 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (z-score: 17.78, the highest anomaly in dataset)
1980% increase represents the most acute spike across all complaint categories
Sustained baseline of only ~10 complaints per 8-week period, making this spike statistically extraordinary
reporting_angles: Are specific neighborhoods in East Flatbush seeing coordinated tagging? Interview residents on which blocks are most affected.
Has the city's graffiti removal contractor fallen behind, or is this a new crew targeting the district?

themes_detail.label: Street conditions deteriorating rapidly
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped to 41 THIS WEEK—a 212% spike from the 13.1-complaint weekly average—signaling possible pothole proliferation, sidewalk damage, or deferred maintenance hitting critical mass in the district.
evidence: 41 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.49)
212% increase coincides with recent weather patterns or winter wear; timing suggests actionable city maintenance gap
Combined with 15 vehicle noise complaints (208% spike) this week, street damage may be causing hazardous conditions
reporting_angles: Map the locations of this week's 41 street complaints—are they clustered on specific avenues or commercial corridors?
Interview DoT on emergency pothole repairs and whether East Flatbush has been deprioritized in maintenance scheduling.

themes_detail.label: Vehicle noise complaints tripled
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints hit 15 THIS WEEK—a 208% surge from the 4.9-complaint weekly average—potentially linked to street deterioration, illegal modifications, or enforcement lapses creating a disruptive environment for residents.
evidence: 15 vehicle noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.28)
208% spike coincides with street condition complaints (41 this week), suggesting potholes/rough roads may amplify engine/exhaust noise
Residential noise remains high at 1,898 complaints over 90 days, but vehicle-specific noise is now accelerating
reporting_angles: Which streets are generating the most complaints? Are illegal muffler modifications or street racing a known problem?
Interview NYPD on noise enforcement capacity and whether East Flatbush is seeing enforcement gaps.

themes_detail.label: Electrical hazards spike 2 weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints peaked at 4 two weeks ago—a 3100% spike from the 0.1-complaint weekly average—representing a critical safety concern if multiple buildings are experiencing live hazards or widespread wiring failures.
evidence: 4 electrical complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 11.72, second-highest anomaly)
3100% spike suggests either acute failures across multiple properties or a suddenly reported endemic issue
Baseline of near-zero complaints makes even small increases statistically extraordinary; 4 complaints represent potential fire/electrocution hazard
reporting_angles: Which buildings or blocks reported the 4 electrical complaints? Are they aging structures with known infrastructure problems?
Interview Con Edison on whether there were grid incidents, transformer failures, or service disruptions in East Flatbush 2 weeks ago.

themes_detail.label: Dead/dying trees spike 2 weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints surged to 6 two weeks ago—a 1100% spike from the 0.5-complaint weekly average—indicating either storm damage, disease, or deferred forestry maintenance affecting the district's tree canopy.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.78)
1100% spike is statistically significant but may reflect delayed reporting of storm damage or seasonal die-off
No follow-up spike this week suggests the issue may have resolved or reporting plateaued
reporting_angles: Were these complaints tied to a specific weather event (wind, freeze) 2–3 weeks prior?
Interview Parks Department on tree removal backlogs and whether East Flatbush has an aging or disease-prone tree inventory.
